Private installed fixture checkpoint; source preparation only.

Red triggers for the inert tests: duplicate manifest keys could silently
retarget an input; unfilled template could qualify an arbitrary binary; changed
archive/image bytes could run after review; escaped input could read outside the
checkout; native interruption/compaction or mismatched execution could count as
terminal attention; an exited but unawaited fixture child could leak ownership.
Tests exercise parser/native-envelope and inert child boundaries. They do not
mock a qualified profile, production clock, native frame grant or external effect.

Manifest paths are repository relative and SHA256-bound. Fill all eleven cells
with exact candidate builds; official archive SHA/SRI/executable identities are
now populated from supplied primary custody facts. The independent compact
`reviewed-host-custody.json` preserves the input/review/primary-metadata hashes and
archive origins; parser checks need no TASK-INPUTS mount and compare both ledgers
against that supplied custody, including all eleven cells. Null candidate
fields and the missing current1.18.34 upstream source commit
fail. `hostSourceCommit` must identify immutable upstream source for that version.
`embedded` and independently `rebuilt` bytes must agree before host launch. Supply
the actual packed SDK tar and its SHA512 SRI, source manifest hash and exact npm
lock bytes. A file tar uses actual `resolved:file:` metadata and may lack integrity;
there is no invented registry integrity. One global bundle/lock applies to all cells.
The runner also compares host inputs to the reviewed byte-only pin ledger.
The manifest is custody input; it cannot grant product runtime eligibility.
Darwin `nativeApp` is `{root,executable:{path,sha256},sidecar:{path,sha256}}`.
Actual installer still checks its seal/signature; fixture hashing is insufficient.

Root runs after integration/review. Commit source first, then build/review that exact
clean revision and seal EXTERNAL parent evidence; never commit a filled final
manifest whose candidate commit/binary hash would depend on itself. Dispatch takes
an HTTPS evidence tar URL and independently reviewed SHA256, no secrets. The tar
contains `manifest.json` plus regular files rooted at the fresh external
`.task-tools/artifacts/parent-inputs/`, using the template's repository-relative
paths. It includes exact native images/official host archives, independently rebuilt
bundle and original SDK/qualification proof records. Reuse the parent's actual
reviewed proof bytes with their exact provenance, not new SDK copies. Embedded JS,
npm lock and its actual vendored file tar remain in the exact checkout; archive
staging cannot replace source. All eleven custody cells stay mandatory.
CI seals the staged manifest SHA, verifies actual Go `vcs.revision`/clean build,
clean tracked checkout/HEAD and every bundle/SDK/artifact hash before any host.
Untracked source files also fail; only `.task-tools/artifacts` is excluded from
that untracked-source check, and the final manifest itself must be untracked.
It compiles only the private receiver, then retains native managed/path checks.
The parent archive/pins are not produced by this worker; absent/wrong evidence
stops CI as unqualified (including unstaged pull requests). Direct root execution
also requires `--manifest-sha256` for the external manifest. These gates are source
assertions, not executed builds or accepted installed evidence. Linux uses a new loopback-only netns,
owned foreground bus and separately built receiver. Source-only worker must never
execute the `ci_inputs.py` command entrypoint, installed/native runner execution, provider, bus or notifier.
Only `test_fixture.py`, AST/Node syntax checks and Go formatting are local checks.
No fixture defaults to user config, auth, bus, provider or existing runtime root.

First concrete gate failure stops later phases with nonzero/unqualified; neither
missing archives nor denied qualification is skip/pass. The baseline product has
no origin token in the embedded bundle, nil profile qualification and empty clock
cells. Current public `config inspect` resolves shared `config.json`, whereas the
managed consumer reads `<control-root>/agent-notifications.json`. It has no path
flag. Runner refuses that mismatch, does not set AGENT_NOTIFICATIONS_CONFIG and
never writes an unlocked policy. The narrow product integration needed is an
existing public config/store path selecting the managed policy with CAS and
compatible generation/lock semantics, retaining setup route fields.

The native capture is an independent read-only observer, not the product observer.
Its real same-parent profile query is bounded and waits for actual close, with no
eligible fields supplied. A production clock snapshot is E0 evidence only; no
public pre-model command currently proves selected complete T/source conversion.
The explicit stop in `qualify` preserves this unresolved gate. Root must resolve
it through authoritative product integration/evidence, never delete it merely to
reach scenarios. The business/lifecycle body below it is staged and unexecuted.

Four pending/final cases require correlated native facts and one desktop call plus
one webhook. Pending attention stays pending until both effects, then closes by
real cancel/reject. Retry/interrupt use frozen P0 native discrimination. Removal
retains the same live host; no restored executable or injected neutral wire.
Update keeps registration, reinstall rotates it; a new loader gets a fresh turn.
Observed counts do not prove absence of later work: final product checkpoint and
owned IPC close remain unproved, so no staged body returns E2E pass.

loader; natural end/error/reconnect/hydration; stale-origin final spawn/close;
lease-linearized revoke/remove and durable uncertain claims; accepted-disconnected
webhook no retry after real duplicate/reload; complete native clock/boot/conversion;

Five platform pairs, floor/V2 plus Linuxamd64 current, remain eleven unrun cells.
Keep ordinary 25s JS/20s Go budgets; no new sleeps establish settlement.
Fixture cleanup closes its tracked accepted HTTP sockets before awaiting request
threads, so partial requests cannot leave a provider/sink reader blocked forever.
The existing8s P0 transport bound applies; partial POSTs are not accepted effects.
This source-only cleanup has no provider/sink runtime evidence here.

Private native/provider traces use HMAC identities and original native numeric
clocks, not receive-time substitutes. Private roots/logs stay under
`.task-tools/artifacts`; public upload contains only the bounded report. No raw
conversation, password, native IDs or prompt text is published. Root creates the
owner commit after handoff; linked external git is unavailable to this worker.

Continuation red triggers: transcribing x64 to an unsupported fixture arch could
drop an ARM or Windows cell; mixing registry/archive and executable hashes could
launch different bytes; treating a copied fork message as fresh could revive old
completion. Parser fixtures compare supplied custody facts and reject excluded
canonical message identities; these tests make no native/runtime grant.

Final-assistant red trigger: a permanent provider400 plus a failed native step
could be counted while its ordinary assistant projection is missing, incomplete,
from another session/message, a compaction summary or a user interruption. The
staged driver must also read the existing public history/context route and match
the native final message identity and original numeric completion time. Independent
parser examples reject those mismatches without invoking any native host or grant.

Review R1 red triggers: a clean source copy lacks hosted TASK-INPUTS; a manifest
tracked with its own exact commit creates an impossible source/artifact cycle;
same native IDs can conceal changed V1 parent/completion metadata. Inert tests
use real private external tar/file IO, separate source/metadata parser examples
and independently supplied V1 envelopes/projections. They prove no real Go build,
clean Git checkout, SDK/native/profile/clock grant or installed effect. V1 compares
original parentID/completed against the independently fetched projection. V2 keeps
its existing native execution/message identities without invented time aliases.
